E_nom: c0 2.94 c1 3.36 c2 4.43 c3 3.00 c4 3.17 c5 1.31 c6 4.08 c7 4.89 pkg 2.36 (mean 3.28) E_skew(c0-3 max,c4-7 min): c0 2.95 c1 2.52 c2 3.89 c3 2.01 c4 2.29 c5 2.47 c6 3.07 c7 2.77 pkg 2.86 (mean 2.76, fairly flat) E_min(m2): ~0. Common mode ~ proportional to total power (nom80W->3.28, skew68W->2.76, min8W->0). IHS laterally well-coupled (lateral IHS R~1-2 << boundary R~5) so a too-low model boundary conductance = common-mode rise ~ total power. Candidate GLOBAL fault. Deviations from common mode: nominal-(3.28): c2 +1.15, c7 +1.61, c6 +0.80, c5 -1.97, c0 -0.34, pkg -0.92 skew-(2.76): c2 +1.13, c3 -0.75, c5 -0.29, others small. c2 elevated +1.1 in BOTH -> real core2 dissipates more than model (model gain too low) OR sensor high. c5 low at nominal only (core5 powered) , near-0 at skew(core5 unpowered) -> model power_gain core5 too HIGH, or T_core5 low-gain. c7 high at nominal only (core7 powered), ~0 at skew -> model power_gain core7 too LOW, or T_core7 high. DESIGN: single-block-max from all-min baseline to isolate each block's own dissipated power vs model. A: core2 max, B: core5 max, C: core7 max. Compare measured rise vs model rise & neighbor consistency (sensor fault shows only on that sensor; gain error shows on neighbors too).

61NoteKEY INSIGHT: The system is linear; scaling ALL edge resistances by k scales every T-rise by exactly k, AND scales transient tau by k. Observed: rises uniformly ~1.09x model, transient tau also longer (~1.1x). => global thermal-resistance underestimation, k~1.09. No single block power_gain can make +3.5C uniform (would need >envelope; each block's sensitivity is peaked, not flat). => GLOBAL model problem. Least-squares k (nominal, all sensors): 1.093 incl c2, 1.087 excl c2. Use k~1.09 (R_real = 1.09*R_model => G_model/G_real = +9%). Residuals after global k=1.09 (nominal): c0-0.5,c1+0.0,c2+1.7,c3+0.4,c4-0.3,c5-0.7,c6+0.7,c7+0.6,pkg+0.6. Only c2 (>spec, borderline). c2 excess only at nominal (high T); ~0 at core2max. Could be small sensor gain err OR noise. Need one more high-temp point. Run cores-max / noncore-min (~92W, near cap) to confirm k with big SNR and re-check c2.

REJECT. - If BOUNDARY R scaled kb: pkg (mostly boundary) scales full; cores (boundary+Rvertical) scale less => pkg E/rise > cores E/rise. MATCHES (pkg 0.106 > cores ~0.09). => fault is ambient/boundary conductance too HIGH (b_* R too LOW) ~10%. - c2 E/rise 0.131 HIGHEST, above boundary prediction => separate T_core2 sensor gain fault candidate (~few %). TEST: scale all 13 b_* R by 1.10, rc_run, compare to averaged nominal/coresmax (excl c2).
68Propose h3Model boundary (ambient/IHS-to-ambient) thermal conductance is too high (~10%): the b_* edge resistances are too low, so the model under-predicts temperature rise. Signature: error/rise fraction is largest at T_package (nearest pure-boundary path) and smaller at cores (which also drop across vertical resistance). Fixable by scaling the 13 b_* resistances.
69NoteCRUCIAL: E_avg vs core commanded power is ~linear: E/Pcore = .057(nom60W),.061(skew45.5W),.068(coresmax90W) ~ const 0.06. vs total power NOT linear. NON-core power: skew has noncore at NOMINAL yet lowest E -> not noncore. => extra heat proportional to CORE power. Real cores dissipate more than model. Also c2 E/rise ~3.5% above its neighbors in BOTH nominal & coresmax, neighbours normal => LOCAL sensor T_core2 gain fault (~+3.5% of rise). Test candidate model faults with FREE rc_run at nominal. 568Propose h4Degraded die-to-ambient cooling: real vertical (die->IHS) AND boundary (IHS->ambient) thermal resistances are ~8.9% higher than the factory model, while lateral spreading (Si-Si and IHS-IHS) is unchanged. This is the physically correct signature of TIM/heat-removal degradation in a chip in service: the series heat-removal path degrades, the in-plane spreading path does not. Predicts uniform-across-sensors temperature rise ~9% above factory, growing with total power. All-R scaling fails (wrongly scales laterals, distorts skew gradients); boundary-only fails (leaves vertical/TIM unscaled). Magnitude G_model/G_real-1 = +0.089.
569NoteMID-POWER DECISIVE DATA (factory v0 predictions r116/117/118 vs meas m30/m33/m34): rise-ratio (real/model) vs total power: 8W:1.00, 32W(m33):1.038, 36W(m30):1.038, 60W(m34):1.069, 68.5W(skew):1.077, 80W(nom):1.086. - m30(cores-min/noncore-max) == m33(cores-half/noncore-min) in E => tracks TOTAL power, NOT per-block. Kills per-block power_gain. - E uniform incl T_package, grows with power => common-mode die->ambient series path. Two failed commits were all-R x1.089 (scales laterals too -> skew bad) and boundary-only x1.11 (leaves vertical/TIM unscaled). Correct physical mechanism = degraded cooling = vertical+boundary scaled, laterals intact (v+b x1.089). Never committed. Untested regime = mid power. TESTING NOW. n/a

Uniform across ALL sensors incl pkg. Transient m6 excess grows as chip heats (1.065 early ->1.10 final). CONCLUSION: real thermal resistance is TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT (nonlinear); a linear RC card can only fit one operating point. Best physical structure = degraded die->ambient SERIES path: vertical TIM (v_*) + boundary (b_*) scaled, laterals intact. This is the ONLY combo never cleanly committed (all-R failed: scales laterals->bad skew; boundary-only failed: leaves vertical/TIM unscaled). Card decision: v+b x1.089 (fits nominal RMS 0.53, skew 0.54, validated r55/56). Report model error at nominal reference = +0.089 (edge conductance model/real-1). Sensor T_core2 gain +0.05 of rise (no offset at min; neighbors not elevated). NEXT: apply 26 v+b x1.089 edits, verify rc_run, commit.

PATTERN: pkg highest (~1.11-1.12); cold/hot cores spread 1.06-1.13. - all-R → uniform ratio (all equal) — REJECTED (pkg higher). - vertical-only → pkg ratio ~1.0 (ihs unchanged) — REJECTED (pkg=1.11). - BOUNDARY-only → pkg ratio ~k, hot cores (big local vertical drop) ratio <k, cold cores ratio near k. EXACTLY MATCHES. => MODEL FAULT = boundary (IHS→ambient) resistance too low / conductance too high. This is what h3 said; boundary×1.11 commit failed ONLY because it carried the spurious c2 sensor row. LOW-POWER maps (min 8W, all-half 40W) show ratio ~1.0-1.03 but rises are small (4-20C) vs quantize 1.0 => low SNR; also set_workload delivery tolerance. Trust high-SNR nominal+skew. c2: ratio 1.131 nominal BUT 1.097 skew (normal!). c2 excess vanishes at skew/mid-power. NOT a constant sensor gain. Under ×1.10 card c2 frac excess: nom .036, skew .011, allhalf .00, .75 .00. => c2 excess is a MODEL misfit localized to c2's site that only appears at nominal map (dense high-power neighbors), likely observation-map crosstalk OR a small core2-region resistance/gain error — NOT a clean sensor gain. Under a correct boundary model, check if c2 residual shrinks into spec. NEXT: revert vertical edges to factory (keep b ×1.10) => boundary-only×1.10. rc_run nominal+skew+allhalf+min. Compare per-sensor. Then solve k from pkg, check c2.
